data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Manual (DM) provides United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) guidance at the Departmental, Mission Area, agency, and staff office levels for:
Requesting and responsibly managing:
Communications and information technology systems used to process or transmit classified national security information (CNSI) throughout its lifecycle; and
Equipment, devices, and cryptographic material for secure communications;
Requesting access to a national security system (NSS) or a network that transmits or processes CNSI;
Moving information between classified and unclassified environments; and
Responding to classified system incidents, spillage of CNSI, and loss of cryptographic keys or secure communication devices or equipment.

This DM serves as the foundation for USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to develop and implement their own procedures for classified systems and CNSI-related activities that comply with Federal and Departmental requirements and are consistent with the overarching guidance provided in this DM.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This DM is in compliance with Executive Order (E.O.) 13526, Classified National Security Information; 32 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 2001, Classified National Security Information Implementing Directive for E.O. 13526; policies and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS); and Intelligence Community Directives (ICD).
cross_references: Executive Order (E.O.) 13526, Classified National Security Information
32 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 2001, Classified National Security Information Implementing Directive for E.O. 13526

policy_statements.source_text: Guidance references are provided in Appendix C, Authorities and References of this document.
This manual is effective immediately and remains in effect until superseded or expired.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their procedures with this manual within 6 months of its publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of its publication date

policy_statements.source_text: This DM applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, subcontractors, and others who work for or on behalf of USDA, and who access or will access CNSI, or support, or will support, an NSS.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, subcontractors, and others who work for or on behalf of USDA, and who access or will access CNSI, or support, or will support, an NSS

policy_statements.source_text: This DM applies to:
All personnel who generate, collect, provide, transmit, store, maintain, or access CNSI on or via Communications Security (COMSEC) equipment or systems by or on behalf of USDA;
NSS or services developed, maintained, or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA;
NSS or services used for accessing, transmitting, or processing CNSI, whether internal to USDA or externally with other Federal agencies or organizations;
Secure, classified communications hardware and software:
Devices and systems such as telephones, mobile devices, video teleconference systems, servers, laptops, desktops, and wireless devices;
Required applications; and
Materials or items designed to secure or authenticate communications, such as cryptographic keys, devices, software, or documents.

Facilities or spaces within a facility, such as a room or floor, that are approved by Office of Homeland Security (OHS) Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD) Classified National Security Information Staff (CNSIS) to house these systems, services, or devices and from which these systems and services operate, whether owned or operated by USDA, or owned or operated on behalf of USDA by a contractor, subcontractor, or other organization; and
Any space, open area, or facility approved and accredited by OHS/PDSD/CNSIS for CNSI activities where portable, secure communication devices are used.
This DM focuses on NSS and CNSI from the perspective of the OHS National Security Systems Program (NSSP).
Other aspects of safeguarding NSS and CNSI are the responsibility of the OHS PDSD, with which OHS NSSP coordinates their activities.
This DM complements Departmental Regulation (DR) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program, and DM 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual.
cross_references: Departmental Regulation (DR) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program
DM 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual

policy_statements.source_text: For more detailed procedures on managing cybersecurity incidents affecting classified systems and CNSI, see DM 3505-005, Cybersecurity Incident Management Procedures.
The following terms are used in this document.
See Appendix C for more detail:

An NSS may also be referred to as a classified system, a classified information system, or a secure communication system that meets the criteria defined in CNSS Instruction (CNSSI) 4009, Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) Glossary.
cross_references: CNSS Instruction (CNSSI) 4009, Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) Glossary

policy_statements.source_text: These terms encompass information systems and telecommunications systems and their components.
For ease of understanding, the term “classified systems” is used in this document.
CNSI may also be referred to as classified information.
Confidential business information and proprietary information are not the same as classified information.
A managed CNSI service is one that is owned or operated by another organization, such as the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), to provide access to or transmission and processing of CNSI.
The procedures in this DM expand on the policies established by DR 3300-015, Secure Communication Systems, which covers:
Appropriate management and control of assets for classified systems and CNSI;
Securing the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of CNSI through coordination with CNSIS;
Coordination of activities at USDA by OHS’s NSSP and OHS, Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and the user community; and
System and device security awareness training for all personnel who access or use COMSEC equipment or support a classified system.

This section explains the procedures for requesting, implementing, using, and operating classified systems and devices, or controlled cryptographic items (CCI) encryption devices, including classified stand-alone systems; equipment used to establish classified data network connectivity or secure video teleconferencing; data encryption devices used to protect CNSI; and secure communication devices used to transmit CNSI, such as fixed, mobile, and satellite telephones and radios.
Procedures for using secure video teleconferencing facilities or accessing classified networks are described in the following Procedures Sections 5c through e.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are responsible for funding the acquisition, implementation, and operations and maintenance (O&M) of these classified devices, as well as the costs for assessment and authorization (A&A).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: acquisition, implementation, and operations and maintenance (O&M) of these classified devices

policy_statements.source_text: All classified systems and their components must be operated in facilities or spaces approved and cleared for CNSI activities by OHS PDSD or by a properly delegated USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office authority, or at a Government facility with which an approved Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) exists by PDSD.
policy_statements.actor_name: All classified systems and their components
policy_statements.target: All classified systems and their components
conditions: in facilities or spaces approved and cleared for CNSI activities by OHS PDSD or by a properly delegated USDA Mission Area, agency, or staff office authority, or at a Government facility with which an approved Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) exists by PDSD

policy_statements.source_text: The standard operating procedures (SOP) for the cleared facility must include procedures to ensure classified systems are stored and operated in accordance with DM 3440-001.
policy_statements.target: standard operating procedures (SOP) for the cleared facility

policy_statements.source_text: Portable secure communication devices, such as mobile phones or radios, must be used in accordance with applicable security doctrine and USDA SOPs when deployed in spaces not formally approved for CNSI activities.
conditions: when deployed in spaces not formally approved for CNSI activities

policy_statements.source_text: The preferred type of classified stand-alone system is a computer with a removable hard drive or laptop that can be stored in a General Services Administration (GSA)-approved security container, which will require that the facility be approved, at a minimum, for closed storage and processing by PDSD.

Computers without removable hard drives, or laptops that are not capable of being stored inside a GSA-approved security container, require the facility to be cleared for open storage of CNSI systems at a classification level equal to or higher than the system.
policy_statements.actor_name: Computers without removable hard drives, or laptops that are not capable of being stored inside a GSA-approved security container

policy_statements.source_text: The requesting agency or staff office must complete the Agriculture Department (AD) Form AD-3084, Justification for a Classified National Security Information System, in which the system owner identifies the requested system or device and provides a detailed justification and system capabilities for the request.
policy_statements.target: Agriculture Department (AD) Form AD-3084, Justification for a Classified National Security Information System
cross_references: Agriculture Department (AD) Form AD-3084, Justification for a Classified National Security Information System

policy_statements.source_text: OHS NSSP works with the system owner to document the “proposed solution”, which details the requirements for the classified system.

The system owner obtains the signatures of the agency funding authority and agency approving authority, indicating that the requesting agency or staff office is able to fund the request, along with the amount of funds available.
policy_statements.target: signatures of the agency funding authority and agency approving authority

policy_statements.source_text: This does not obligate the funds; it only identifies the requestor’s ability to fund the request and ongoing O&M capabilities.
The requesting agency or staff office submits the signed Form AD-3084 to OHS NSSP, which routes the form to OHS PDSD for review and signature.
OHS PDSD reviews the proposed solution requests within 20 business days of receipt to determine if the requesting entity can properly safeguard CNSI.
conditions: within 20 business days of receipt

policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD’s review is based on the:
Intended purpose of the system and use of classified information;
Secure storage requirements and capabilities (where and how storage will be maintained);
Security accreditation of the facility and the facility SOP;
Security operating guidelines for the equipment;
Appropriate security clearances for personnel; and
Documented risk assessment.
OHS PDSD, in its review, identifies the security processes and procedures required before implementation of the proposed system.
policy_statements.target: security processes and procedures required before implementation of the proposed system

policy_statements.source_text: The requirements may apply to the requestor, the OHS NSSP Manager (NSSPM) or OHS NSSP, or a managed CNSI service provider.
OHS PDSD validates that security requirements exist prior to the introduction of the proposed system into an accredited space.
conditions: prior to the introduction of the proposed system into an accredited space

policy_statements.source_text: The Director or designee of OHS either approves or disapproves the request to implement the system or solution.
policy_statements.target: request to implement the system or solution

policy_statements.source_text: The Designated Approval Authority (DAA) reviews the form, certifies through signature that the Information Assurance Risk Management process, in accordance with CNSSI 1253, Security Categorization and Control Selection for National Security Systems, has been completed, and indicates whether the system must undergo A&A.
cross_references: CNSSI 1253, Security Categorization and Control Selection for National Security Systems

policy_statements.source_text: Once the solution is approved, OHS NSSP assists the system owner with following proper acquisition procedures; beginning the A&A process, if required; and implementing the solution.
conditions: Once the solution is approved
if required

policy_statements.source_text: All CCI-type devices and COMSEC materials must be delivered to the USDA COMSEC Manager, who generates Standard Form (SF) 153, COMSEC Material Report, and issues the device(s) to the authorized hand receipt holder.
policy_statements.target: All CCI-type devices and COMSEC materials

policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD updates the facility equipment inventory when the solution is implemented.
conditions: when the solution is implemented

policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD also reviews the SOPs for the facility and any SOPs for the system.
policy_statements.target: SOPs for the facility and any SOPs for the system

policy_statements.source_text: Most systems, components, and devices requested are accredited by a Federal partner agency or managed CNSI service provider.
The USDA DAA for CNSI systems determines whether to accept the external A&A under reciprocity or to require an internal A&A and documents the decision on AD-3084.
The common exception to this is for stand-alone computer systems.
For other exceptions, contact the OHS NSSPM.
The system owner must develop and maintain a detailed system security plan (SSP) for any classified system requiring A&A.
conditions: for any classified system requiring A&A

policy_statements.source_text: The SSP must follow the format and contain the controls outlined in the Master System Security Plan (MSSP) generated by the OHS NSSPM.
CNSSI 1253F Attachment 1, Security Overlays Template, identifies the controls for a NSS, based on its security categorization.
CNSSI 1253F Attachment 5, Classified Information Overlay, provides additional controls for safeguarding CNSI.
The OHS NSSPM and OHS PDSD must review and concur on the SSP.
The system must successfully undergo a formal A&A before it may be used for operations.
conditions: before it may be used for operations

policy_statements.source_text: If there are two classified stand-alone systems, where one is the primary and the other is the alternate or backup, they may be assessed and authorized together as part of a single A&A.
conditions: If there are two classified stand-alone systems, where one is the primary and the other is the alternate or backup

policy_statements.source_text: Certifiers (the personnel who perform the assessment) must have appropriate security clearances, applicable security training, and approved accounts for the systems to be assessed.
When performing the assessment, the certifiers will determine whether the system is properly configured and complies with stated requirements and produce a security assessment report for the DAA.
conditions: When performing the assessment

policy_statements.source_text: Other outputs of the A&A process are the plans of action and milestones (POA&M) to correct any weaknesses identified during the assessment.
In addition to A&A, the Mission Area, agency, or staff office must complete and submit Form AD-3081, Classified Stand-alone Computer Registration/Certification to the USDA COMSEC Manager.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office
policy_statements.target: Form AD-3081, Classified Stand-alone Computer Registration/Certification
cross_references: Form AD-3081, Classified Stand-alone Computer Registration/Certification

policy_statements.source_text: The form provides information about the system and personnel and includes attestations about the facility, system, and personnel.
Relying on the security assessment report and representations on Form AD-3081 by OHS PDSD and the certifiers, the DAA makes a risk-based decision on whether to allow the system to operate.
The DAA’s signature on Form AD-3081 authorizes processing of CNSI on the system and serves as the authorization to operate (ATO).
policy_statements.target: processing of CNSI on the system

policy_statements.source_text: The authorization will be valid for no longer than 3 years, although the DAA may set a shorter time.
conditions: for no longer than 3 years

policy_statements.source_text: Use of classified devices or equipment is restricted to authorized personnel with appropriate security clearances.
policy_statements.target: Use of classified devices or equipment

policy_statements.source_text: All users, system administrators, and certifiers must complete initial classified user training and refresher security training.
policy_statements.actor_name: All users, system administrators, and certifiers
policy_statements.target: initial classified user training and refresher security training

policy_statements.source_text: For classified stand-alone systems:
Both of the following forms must be completed, submitted, and approved for user, system administrator, and certifier accounts on classified stand-alone computers:
Form AD-3085, Classified Stand-Alone Computer User Account Authorization; and

policy_statements.source_text: Form AD-3080, Classified Stand-Alone Computer User Agreement.

policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD approves Form AD-3085.
The system owner and the Mission Area, agency, or staff office security official approve Form AD-3080.
policy_statements.actor_name: system owner and the Mission Area, agency, or staff office security official

policy_statements.source_text: All personnel are required to use different passwords for classified and unclassified system accounts.
policy_statements.target: different passwords for classified and unclassified system accounts

policy_statements.source_text: They are also required to use different passwords for accounts on classified systems that have different classification levels (i.e., the password for a system at the Top Secret level must be different from the password for a system at the Secret level).
policy_statements.target: different passwords for accounts on classified systems that have different classification levels

policy_statements.source_text: Only an individual with a security clearance equal to or higher than the classification of information on the system may serve as system administrator.
policy_statements.actor_name: individual with a security clearance equal to or higher than the classification of information on the system
conditions: with a security clearance equal to or higher than the classification of information on the system

policy_statements.source_text: A certifier must have a security clearance equal to or higher than the classification of information on the system and is prohibited from serving as system administrator or user.
policy_statements.target: classification of information on the system

policy_statements.source_text: System users are prohibited from performing or having system administration privileges.

When a user, certifier, or system administrator is no longer eligible for an account on a classified stand-alone system, the system owner must complete Form AD-3082, Classified Stand-Alone Computer User Account Termination.
policy_statements.target: Form AD-3082, Classified Stand-Alone Computer User Account Termination
conditions: When a user, certifier, or system administrator is no longer eligible for an account on a classified stand-alone system
cross_references: Form AD-3082, Classified Stand-Alone Computer User Account Termination

policy_statements.source_text: As part of the process, a system administrator must attest on the AD-3082 form that the account has been deactivated or removed.

If the official recipient (i.e., the hand receipt holder) of a classified device, equipment, or material is being transferred or reassigned, or will be absent for more than 30 calendar days, the system owner must contact the USDA COMSEC Manager to return the equipment.
conditions: If the official recipient (i.e., the hand receipt holder) of a classified device, equipment, or material is being transferred or reassigned, or will be absent for more than 30 calendar days

policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD must be informed to update the equipment inventory.
If the device or material is needed by another individual, only the USDA COMSEC Manager is authorized to re-issue and transfer the material.
conditions: If the device or material is needed by another individual

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA COMSEC Manager will arrange for a secure transfer of the device or equipment and delegation of responsibility prior to the official recipient’s departure.
conditions: prior to the official recipient’s departure

policy_statements.source_text: If the equipment is to be transferred to another location, PDSD must pre-approve and accredit the space where the device is to be located.
policy_statements.target: space where the device is to be located
conditions: If the equipment is to be transferred to another location

policy_statements.source_text: Failure to properly return or transfer the device or equipment prior to departure may result in a reportable COMSEC incident.
When a device or equipment is no longer needed, the system owner must return it to the USDA COMSEC Manager, with a completed SF153.
conditions: When a device or equipment is no longer needed

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA COMSEC Manager must properly inventory and account for returned items before they can be re-issued.
conditions: before they can be re-issued

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not authorized to re-issue or key the device or equipment to another individual.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: To remove or relocate classified non-mobile devices or equipment, the system owner must complete and submit form SF153 to the USDA COMSEC Manager.
conditions: To remove or relocate classified non-mobile devices or equipment

policy_statements.source_text: If equipment needs to be relocated, the system owner must provide at least 30 calendar days’ advance notice to the USDA COMSEC Manager.
conditions: If equipment needs to be relocated
at least 30 calendar days’ advance notice

policy_statements.source_text: This allows time for NSSP coordination with OHS PDSD to address any logistical changes or security concerns.
Only authorized personnel with appropriate security clearance can remove or relocate the devices or equipment.
policy_statements.actor_name: authorized personnel with appropriate security clearance
conditions: with appropriate security clearance

policy_statements.source_text: As part of ongoing operations, OHS PDSD reviews and approves equipment inventories for the secure facility or space, and conducts compliance and oversight inspections.
policy_statements.target: equipment inventories for the secure facility or space

policy_statements.source_text: This section discusses procedures for moving data or information between unclassified and classified domains, or from one security domain level to another, such as from unclassified to Secret or from Secret to Top Secret.
A security domain is an environment within system entities that have a single classification or sensitivity level operating under a common security policy, security model, or security architecture.
Classification levels include unclassified, controlled, Secret, Top Secret, and Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI).
Only sanitized information on a printed document may be transferred from a classified to an unclassified environment, following these steps:
policy_statements.target: sanitized information on a printed document

policy_statements.source_text: Create and print a sanitized version of the document by removing all classified information from the document, so the resulting document contains only statements with unclassified (U) markings and insert headers and footers to designate the document as unclassified.
Two authorized individuals must review the printed document to verify that the document contains no classified information.
One of those individuals scans the document to the unclassified network, using an unclassified device.
Information being transferred from an unclassified environment to a classified network or system must be in the form of a printed document.
policy_statements.target: Information being transferred from an unclassified environment to a classified network or system

policy_statements.source_text: Use a scanner connected to the classified network or system to upload the printed unclassified document.
Retrieve the document electronically on the classified network or system after the transfer is complete.
conditions: after the transfer is complete

policy_statements.source_text: Information being transferred from a lower-level classified environment to a higher-level classified network or system must be in the form of a printed document.
policy_statements.target: Information being transferred from a lower-level classified environment to a higher-level classified network or system

policy_statements.source_text: Use a scanner connected to the higher-level classified network or system to upload the printed document.
Retrieve the document electronically on the higher-level classified network or system after the transfer is complete.
conditions: after the transfer is complete

policy_statements.source_text: Obtain and follow the instructions for the managed CNSI service provider’s method and tools for transferring information.
policy_statements.target: instructions for the managed CNSI service provider’s method and tools for transferring information

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS NSSP staff supports all secure video teleconferencing systems (SVTS) for USDA and maintains the SOPs for SVTS operation and use.
USDA has two types of SVTS systems.
The Homeland Secure Data Network (HSDN) SVTS is located in Washington, DC, and planned for other locations.
The Crisis Management System SVTS is located in various USDA facilities.
Contact OHS NSSP for further information.
Users who need to attend or host a classified secure video teleconference must submit a completed PDSD Reservation Request Form.
policy_statements.actor_name: Users who need to attend or host a classified secure video teleconference
conditions: who need to attend or host a classified secure video teleconference

policy_statements.source_text: The form can be requested from PDSD or NSSP.
Submit the form via email to <CNSIS@usda.gov> and <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov> 3 business days prior to the scheduled event.
conditions: 3 business days prior to the scheduled event

policy_statements.source_text: PDSD will verify if the space is available, the participants have the appropriate clearance level, and they are allowed unescorted access to the facility.
NSSP will coordinate the logistics of the call after PDSD confirms space availability and participant clearance levels.
conditions: after PDSD confirms space availability and participant clearance levels

policy_statements.source_text: HSDN is the Secret-level wide area network, owned and managed by DHS, that provides Federal agencies involved in homeland security missions with access to classified information.
HSDN services include full-service network operations, collaboration tools, enterprise applications, and common workstation configurations.
Personnel who require access to HSDN must apply for an account, which may also be used to access classified State Department cables.
policy_statements.actor_name: Personnel who require access to HSDN
conditions: who require access to HSDN

policy_statements.source_text: OHS NSSP assists USDA personnel by processing requests for HSDN access and interfacing with DHS on their behalf.
All requests for HSDN accounts or HSDN support in general must be sent to the HSDN Support Team in OHS NSSP.
policy_statements.target: HSDN Support Team in OHS NSSP

policy_statements.source_text: The user must work with their information security (IS) Coordinator and PDSD to complete initial and biannual Derivative Classification Training.
policy_statements.target: initial and biannual Derivative Classification Training

policy_statements.source_text: The new user must complete Form AD-3083, Justification Request for an HSDN Account, and obtain the signature of their supervisor.
policy_statements.target: Form AD-3083, Justification Request for an HSDN Account
cross_references: Form AD-3083, Justification Request for an HSDN Account

policy_statements.source_text: The completed form must be submitted electronically to via e-mail <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov>.
OHS NSSP will forward the completed AD-3083 form to the approving authority or the person to whom that authority has been delegated.
For HSDN accounts, that authority has been delegated to the OHS PDSD Chief, the Special Security Officer (SSO), and alternate SSO.
If the requestor has not received a response within 5 business days, contact OHS NSSP at <USDA-HSDN-SupportTeam@usda.gov> or 202-720-0594.
conditions: If the requestor has not received a response within 5 business days

policy_statements.source_text: A user approved for an HSDN account will receive DHS’s HSDN Account Request Application Package to complete.
policy_statements.target: DHS’s HSDN Account Request Application Package
cross_references: DHS’s HSDN Account Request Application Package

policy_statements.source_text: The HSDN Support Team is available to assist.
Only designated OHS PDSD personnel may complete the Component Security Clearance Verification Block and Derivative Classification Training Block.
policy_statements.target: Component Security Clearance Verification Block and Derivative Classification Training Block

policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD can provide a list of personnel authorized to sign the form.
policy_statements.target: list of personnel authorized to sign the form

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, agency, and staff office IS Coordinators are not authorized to sign the form.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office IS Coordinators

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS NSSPM and Deputy NSSPM are authorized to sign the component Mission Area, agency, or staff office’s representative block.
policy_statements.target: component Mission Area, agency, or staff office’s representative block

policy_statements.source_text: Upon approval, the HSDN user will be issued a public key infrastructure (PKI) token and must set a personal identification number (PIN) to access HSDN.
conditions: Upon approval

policy_statements.source_text: For questions or issues with the token, or to set or reset the PIN, contact the HSDN Support Team at <USDA-HSDN-SupportTeam@usda.gov> or 202-720-0594.
Another Federal partner department or agency may issue an HSDN PKI token, with prior coordination between the USDA point of contact (POC) for PKI and the other department’s PKI POC.
policy_statements.actor_name: Another Federal partner department or agency
conditions: with prior coordination between the USDA point of contact (POC) for PKI and the other department’s PKI POC

policy_statements.source_text: HSDN users are required to login to their accounts every 30 calendar days to maintain an active account.
conditions: every 30 calendar days

policy_statements.source_text: DHS manages HSDN accounts as follows:
The account is locked after 45 calendar days of inactivity; and
conditions: after 45 calendar days of inactivity

policy_statements.source_text: The account is deactivated after 180 calendar days of inactivity.
conditions: after 180 calendar days of inactivity

policy_statements.source_text: A user whose account is locked or deactivated must contact the HSDN Support Team at <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov> or 202-720-0594.
policy_statements.actor_name: user whose account is locked or deactivated
conditions: whose account is locked or deactivated

policy_statements.source_text: The HSDN PKI token is the property of DHS and is considered a high-value unclassified item.
The PIN is classified at the Secret level.
The token and PIN are solely for the use of the person to whom the token is issued and must not be shared with anyone else.
The token may not be used on an unclassified system; doing so constitutes a reportable violation.
conditions: on an unclassified system

policy_statements.source_text: Taking the token into a foreign country or into the embassy or consulate of another country is a reportable security violation.

Loss, loss of control, suspected or actual compromise of the token, or compromise of the PIN must be reported within 24 hours of detection to OHS NSSP at <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov> or 202-720-0594.
policy_statements.target: Loss, loss of control, suspected or actual compromise of the token, or compromise of the PIN
conditions: within 24 hours of detection

policy_statements.source_text: The token must be returned to OHS NSSP upon termination of the account.
conditions: upon termination of the account

policy_statements.source_text: Notify OHS NSSP within 24 hours when:
An HSDN account is no longer needed because the account holder is terminating employment or changing job responsibilities;
The security clearance status of the account holder changes; or
Use of the account must be restricted for reasons such as conducting an inquiry.
OHS NSSP processes the account termination or suspension with DHS and restricts access to HSDN facilities.
OHS NSSP operates the HSDN Suite access for the convenience of personnel from Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that have HSDN accounts.

The USDA South Building, room S100-E, in Washington, DC, is available during normal duty hours, Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. (Eastern Time), excluding Federal holidays, times of approved early release, closure of the Federal Government, or closure of the South Building; and
HSDN users in Washington, DC, with an urgent need for HSDN access outside normal duty hours may go to the USDA Security Operations Center, South Building, room S310.
policy_statements.actor_name: HSDN users in Washington, DC, with an urgent need for HSDN access outside normal duty hours
policy_statements.target: USDA Security Operations Center, South Building, room S310
conditions: in Washington, DC, with an urgent need for HSDN access outside normal duty hours

policy_statements.source_text: Other USDA facilities with HSDN access are:
The Beacon facility in Kansas City, MO;
The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) headquarters facility in the National Capitol Region;
The Emergency Relocation Facility in Elkins, WV; and
The APHIS facility in Fort Collins, CO.
DHS maintains HSDN access at Fusion Centers across the United States.
OHS NSSP can provide a list of these locations.
To obtain access to a Fusion Center, the following steps are required in advance:
Contact OHS NSSP at <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov> or 202-720-0594 to coordinate the access request; and
Contact OHS PDSD at <cnsis@usda.gov> or 202-720-7373.
OHS PDSD will:
Determine if an agreement is required between USDA and DHS for access and, if so, put the agreement in place; and
conditions: if so

policy_statements.source_text: Pass the user’s personnel security clearance verification information to the Fusion Center.

policy_statements.source_text: The Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System (JWICS) for processing and transmitting TS/SCI is operated by a managed CNSI service provider.
OHS PDSD personnel serve as the local administrators for this system and handle all aspects of the system and customer support other than cryptographic support.
OHS NSSP provides cryptographic support functions for JWICS.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to fund their allocated percentage of the annual O&M costs for JWICS access, working through OHS NSSP, which coordinates with the managed CNSI service provider.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: their allocated percentage of the annual O&M costs for JWICS access

policy_statements.source_text: To obtain JWICS access:
Request initial JWICS access by contacting OHS PDSD at <cnsis@usda.gov> or 202-720-7373;
Complete the JWICS request account package and submit it to OHS PDSD; and
The Director or Deputy Director of OHS will review the submitted package to approve or disapprove the request.
policy_statements.actor_name: Director or Deputy Director of OHS

policy_statements.source_text: To modify or terminate JWICS access, contact OHS PDSD at <cnsis@usda.gov> or 202-720-7373.
This section provides a high-level summary of essential information regarding incidents affecting classified systems, spillage of CNSI, and loss of cryptographic keys or COMSEC devices or equipment.
More extensive details can be found in DM 3440-001 and, for CNSI spillage, DM 3505-005.

When reporting a classified or potentially classified incident, including spillage of CNSI, utilize operational security discipline for all communication, to minimize further exposure of the incident and damage to CNSI.
conditions: When reporting a classified or potentially classified incident, including spillage of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Specifically:
Provide only the minimum amount of information to convey that there has been an incident, then request a face-to-face meeting or a secure call;
policy_statements.target: minimum amount of information to convey that there has been an incident

policy_statements.source_text: Avoid indicating what the information is or its classification, unless using approved secure methods of communication; and
policy_statements.target: what the information is or its classification
conditions: unless using approved secure methods of communication

policy_statements.source_text: Only discuss the incident or potential incident with personnel who have a need to know.
conditions: who have a need to know

policy_statements.source_text: The physical loss of a cryptographic key, COMSEC device, or other secure communication system or component used to process CNSI must be reported within 12 hours of discovery to:
conditions: within 12 hours of discovery

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA COMSEC Manager via OHS NSSP; and
OHS PDSD.
All actual or suspected cybersecurity incidents affecting a classified system or CNSI must be reported immediately upon discovery, or notification of the incident, to the:
conditions: immediately upon discovery, or notification of the incident

policy_statements.source_text: Office of the Chief Information Officer – Information Security Center – Cyber Defense Operations Division (OCIO-ISC-CDOD);
OHS PDSD;
Agency or staff office IS Coordinators, if applicable; and
conditions: if applicable

policy_statements.source_text: Agency or staff office information security support staff.
The OHS SSO also reports incidents to the OCIO-ISC-CDOD.
OCIO-ISC-CDOD: Email <cyber.incidents@usda.gov> or call 866-905-6890; both are staffed 24x7x365.
OHS PDSD: Email <cnsis@usda.gov> or call 202-720-7373; the phone is staffed Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. until 5 p.m. (Eastern Time).
The USDA COMSEC Manager via OHS NSSP: Email <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@usda.gov> or call 202-720-0594.
OHS PDSD:
Determines whether an official investigation is necessary;
Contacts the data owner and agrees on steps needed for cleanup; and
Notifies and coordinates with the security staff of any affected external network provider.
policy_statements.target: security staff of any affected external network provider

policy_statements.source_text: OHS NSSP:
Assists and advises in the incident containment and cleanup strategies and activities, if CNSI systems are involved;
policy_statements.target: incident containment and cleanup strategies and activities
conditions: if CNSI systems are involved

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinates with classified network owners, as appropriate; and
conditions: as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Submits a report to OHS PDSD.
The OCIO-ISC-CDOD:
Coordinates with OHS PDSD on the approved incident containment and cleanup processes; and
Manages the incident containment and cleanup by:
Investigating the spread of the incident and communicating that information to OHS PDSD; and

Notifying and advising USDA network owners, external network providers, and network administrators how to contain the incident, isolate and protect classified or potentially classified information, and clean up the incident.
policy_statements.target: USDA network owners, external network providers, and network administrators

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of the OHS, in the capacity as DAA, will:
Review and approve Form AD-3084;
Certify that the Information Assurance Risk Management process has been completed and indicate whether the system must undergo A&A;
Upon completion of A&A, make a risk-based decision on allowing the system to operate; and
conditions: Upon completion of A&A

policy_statements.source_text: Sign Form AD-3081 to authorize processing of CNSI on the system.
The OHS NSSPM serving as the USDA COMSEC Manager will:
Review and concur on SSPs for classified systems;
Coordinate with managed CNSI service providers; and
Sign as the component agency representative on requests for HSDN accounts.
The OHS NSSP Manager will:
Assist the system owner or requestor with documenting detailed requirements and the proposed solution for the system;
Assist the system owner with implementing the approved solution;
Coordinate with SVTS facility owners and requestors to schedule secure video teleconferences;
Verify PDSD has confirmed all attendees’ clearances prior to the start of any secure video teleconference;
conditions: prior to the start of any secure video teleconference

policy_statements.source_text: Operate facilities for HSDN access;
Guide users who need access to classified communications systems at Fusion Centers to OHS/PDSD, which will assist in establishing an MOU;
policy_statements.target: users who need access to classified communications systems at Fusion Centers

policy_statements.source_text: Manage HSDN account requests, account terminations and suspensions, and related support processes;
policy_statements.target: HSDN account requests, account terminations and suspensions, and related support processes

policy_statements.source_text: Provide cryptographic support functions for JWICS;
Provide initial and annual refresher communications system user security training for authorized users; and
Assist and advise in containment and cleanup, and coordinate with classified network owners, as appropriate, when an actual or suspected cybersecurity incident is reported.
conditions: as appropriate
when an actual or suspected cybersecurity incident is reported

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS Director or Deputy Director will:
Review and approve or disapprove requests for implementing a classified system or device, based on information from the review by OHS NSSP and OHS PDSD, and JWICS access.
policy_statements.target: requests for implementing a classified system or device

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS PDSD Chief will:
Review and approve or disapprove requests for new CNSI systems and HSDN accounts.
policy_statements.target: requests for new CNSI systems and HSDN accounts

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS PDSD Division Chief will:

Review the proposed solution for a requested system or device, and identify security processes and procedures required to implement the system before approving the introduction of the proposed system into an accredited space;
policy_statements.target: proposed solution for a requested system or device
conditions: before approving the introduction of the proposed system into an accredited space

policy_statements.source_text: Review and concur on the SSP for the system;
Maintain, review, and approve equipment inventories for secure facilities or spaces;
policy_statements.target: equipment inventories for secure facilities or spaces

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct compliance and oversight inspections of facilities and spaces containing classified systems and equipment;
policy_statements.target: facilities and spaces containing classified systems and equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Manage Fusion Center agreements through DHS, and provide Fusion Centers with security clearance information for properly cleared personnel who require access;
conditions: who require access

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as local administrators for JWICS, manage JWICS account accesses and terminations, and provide general JWICS customer support; and

Determine whether an official investigation is necessary when an actual or suspected cybersecurity incident is reported, coordinate with the data owner on cleanup strategies, and notify and coordinate with the security staff of any affected external network.
conditions: when an actual or suspected cybersecurity incident is reported

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Funding Authority and Approving Authority will:
Sign Form AD-3084 indicating the ability to fund the request and the amount of funds available.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office Funding Authority and Approving Authority

policy_statements.source_text: The System Owner or Requestor must:
Complete Form AD-3084 and obtain signoff from the Mission Area, agency, or staff office funding authority and approving authority;
Budget for initial and reoccurring A&A of the requested system, unless the system or device is already accredited by another Federal agency;
conditions: unless the system or device is already accredited by another Federal agency

policy_statements.source_text: Develop a concept of operations (CONOPS) for the requested system;
Collaborate with OHS NSSP to document the detailed requirements and proposed solution for the system;
policy_statements.target: detailed requirements and proposed solution for the system

policy_statements.source_text: Develop and maintain a detailed SSP for the system;
Ensure that the system A&A is completed, with all weaknesses corrected or documented as POA&Ms, prior to system implementation or operation;
conditions: prior to system implementation or operation

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that all users, system administrators, and certifiers complete all required security training pertinent to the system;
policy_statements.target: all users, system administrators, and certifiers

policy_statements.source_text: Approve accounts for users, system administrators, and certifiers, and ensure that accounts are terminated in a timely manner when someone is or may no longer be eligible for an account; and
policy_statements.target: accounts for users, system administrators, and certifiers
conditions: when someone is or may no longer be eligible for an account

policy_statements.source_text: Submit SF153 to the USDA COMSEC Manager to install, relocate, or remove classified devices or equipment, at least 30 calendar days in advance for relocations.
conditions: at least 30 calendar days in advance for relocations

policy_statements.source_text: Certifiers must:
Assess whether the system is properly configured and complies with stated requirements; and
Produce a security assessment report for the DAA.
Authorized users will:
Complete all required security training, both initially and annually, pertinent to the system;
Use assigned accounts properly, protect passwords, PINs, and tokens, and return tokens to OHS NSSP upon termination of HSDN accounts;
conditions: upon termination of HSDN accounts

policy_statements.source_text: Promptly report to OHS NSSP any loss, loss of control, suspected or actual compromise of an HSDN token, or compromise of an HSDN PIN;
Promptly report the loss of a cryptographic key, COMSEC device, or other secure communication system or component to the USDA COMSEC Manager via OHS NSSP, and to OHS PDSD;
policy_statements.target: USDA COMSEC Manager via OHS NSSP

policy_statements.source_text: Promptly report all actual or suspected cybersecurity incidents affecting a classified system or CNSI to (at a minimum) the OCIO-ISC-CDOD, OHS PDSD, and the Mission Area, agency, or staff office IS Coordinator; and
policy_statements.target: OCIO-ISC-CDOD, OHS PDSD, and the Mission Area, agency, or staff office IS Coordinator

policy_statements.source_text: Follow proper procedures for transferring information to or from a classified environment.
The OCIO-ISC-CDOD must, when an actual or suspected classified cybersecurity incident is reported:
conditions: when an actual or suspected classified cybersecurity incident is reported

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with OHS PDSD on the approved incident containment and cleanup processes;
conditions: when an actual or suspected classified cybersecurity incident is reported

policy_statements.source_text: Investigate the spread of the incident and communicate that information to OHS PDSD; and
conditions: when an actual or suspected classified cybersecurity incident is reported

policy_statements.source_text: Notify and advise USDA network owners, external network providers, and network administrators how to contain the incident, protect CNSI, and clean up the incident.
policy_statements.target: USDA network owners, external network providers, and network administrators
conditions: when an actual or suspected classified cybersecurity incident is reported

policy_statements.target: OHS NSSPM or the HSDN team

The token and PIN are solely for the use of the person to whom the token is issued and must not be shared with anyone else.
The token may not be used on an unclassified system; doing so constitutes a reportable violation.
Taking the token into a foreign country or into the embassy or consulate of another country is a reportable security violation.
